correctness.rationale: From observed minimal three-one and two-one factor lengths recover b+c and min(b,c), and from maximal two-one length recover max(a,d); known n then recovers the unordered inner and outer zero-gap pairs. The only remaining independent assignments have different maximal single-one length unless A>D, B>C, C>=A. The 4-parameter bijection n=7+4t+3u+2v+r counts four-word fibers by partitions into 1,2,3,4, while reflection Burnside gives the class formula and 1/6 limiting ambiguity. All gap-zero, palindrome, n=3 boundary cases are handled. Reconstructed all claims from actual RESULT.md and inspected VERIFY.py; independently enumerated actual substring composition sets for all 1,820 weight-three words of lengths 3..15, including equivalence classes, ambig criterion and counting polynomial. Finite check corroborates, unrestricted proof is gap-statistic argument.

evidence: Published selective three-marker theorem proves reconstruction from P0,P1,P3 with multiplicities and allows two reversal classes from P0,P3; its P1 polynomials distinguish those classes.
Cunha–Medina studies index query construction for a Parikh-vector SET, not inverse-fiber classification.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Retaining multiplicity makes the selective-composition observation strictly richer than the submitted all-layer SET observation. In particular two words can have equal Parikh sets while distinct P1 multiplicity polynomials; the earlier reconstruction theorem does not imply set-fiber uniqueness or count.

evidence: Universal prefix-normal equivalence requires a new weight-three gap and L1 comparison to recover four-fibers; selective P0/P3/P1 theorem has positional multiplicities that separate words even when their sets agree.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Neither inspected source implies the submitted all-length inverse set-fiber theorem merely by substituting parameters or transposing the measurement; a novel combinatorial classification and count remains. Priority nevertheless provisional against unindexed earlier cases.

evidence: Burcsi et al., On Prefix Normal Words and Prefix Normal Forms, Section 2 associates a unique 0- and 1-prefix normal form to each Parikh-set observation; Section 4.2 counts ONE prefix-normal form at fixed density, not joint fibers.
Submitted proof classifies paired gap orderings and counts merges of reversal orbits.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The natural alias is equality of the pair of maximum-zero and maximum-one functions (two prefix normal forms). That universal equivalence alone does not state the exact weight-three inverse-image spectrum; direct formula comparison reveals no covering count.

originality.rationale: Exact joint Parikh-set inverse-fiber classification at binary weight three survives best-of-knowledge comparisons. General paired-prefix-normal-form characterization describes equality of Parikh sets but does not give the four-gap ambiguity criterion, four-element fibers, p_{<=4}(n-7) correction or 1/6 proportion; selective substring-composition result retains multiplicities and therefore solves a strictly stronger observation/reconstruction channel with different fibers.
residual_risks: An unindexed exact weight-three jumbled-equivalence census could predate this search; no universal novelty certificate.
Prefix normal form theory could imply the result after further nontrivial case analysis but does not present its exact gap statistics or counts in inspected material.
